Senses.Explanation: One’s own words from one’s own mouth marks a statement as that same person’s direct, firsthand saying. In Chan interviews it is itself returned as an answer or as a compact certification of what the other person has just said. Miyun gives it as the whole answer to two different questions; Feiyin applies it first to a layman’s conclusion and then to Feng’s charge that Feiyin has fallen into words.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: One’s own words from one’s own mouth marks a statement as that same person’s direct, firsthand saying. In Chan interviews it is itself returned as an answer or as a compact certification of what the other person has just said.
EvidenceBody: Miyun gives it as the whole answer to two different questions; Feiyin applies it first to a layman’s conclusion and then to Feng’s charge that Feiyin has fallen into words.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: An ordinary formula for firsthand testimony becomes a reusable interview verdict that can answer a question or certify the interlocutor’s own line.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase does not prove that the certified statement is true outside its encounter; it identifies whose mouth supplied it.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: 親 repeats the same first-person ownership across speech and mouth; answer and certification are roles of one formula.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The probes retain own speech, mouth, firsthand statement, and direct testimony.

ModifierControls.Finding: The repeated 親 binds both 言 and 口 to the same speaker.

FamilyControls.Finding: The shorter expression names personal utterance without the balanced formula.
